entities.summary: Bāṇabhaṭṭa was a 7th-century Sanskrit prose writer and poet from India. He was the court poet of Emperor Harsha, during his reign at Kanyakubja. Bāna's principal works include a biography of Harsha, the Harshacharita and the novel Kadambari. Bāṇa died before finishing the novel and it was completed by his son Bhūṣaṇabhaṭṭa. Both these works are noted texts of Sanskrit literature. The other works attributed to him are the Caṇḍikāśataka and a drama, the Pārvatīpariṇaya. Banabhatta gets an applause as "Banochhistam Jagatsarvam" meaning Bana has described everything in this world and nothing is left.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a court poet of Emperor Harsha, Bāṇabhaṭṭa's works, such as the Harshacharita and Kadambari, provide valuable insights into medieval Indian literature and culture. His novel Kadambari is considered one of the greatest Sanskrit novels of all time.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a court poet of Emperor Harsha, Bāṇabhaṭṭa's works, such as the Harshacharita and Kadambari, provide valuable insights into medieval Indian literature and politics. His writings had a lasting impact on Sanskrit literature, shaping the literary landscape of ancient India.
